bug_info.bug_desc: The counter error condition cnt_err, generated by the redundant counter (prim_count), was only handled inside the StTx and StTxLast case branches. If cnt_err asserted while the FSM was in any other state such as StIdle, StOpWait, StClean, or the default state, state_d was not forced to StError. As a result, an illegal counter/sequencing condition did not consistently trigger the terminal fatal sequencing error state, so fsm_error_o was not asserted and the module could continue the transaction instead of entering StError as required by spec section 4.4.
bug_info.fix_hint: Move the cnt_err check out of the individual FSM case branches and place it after the end of the case statement as an unconditional next-state override: if cnt_err is asserted, force state_d to StError regardless of the current state. Remove the earlier state-local cnt_err checks so the fatal sequencing transition is evaluated every cycle.
